items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I made some records with J. C. and Doc Cheatham, with Ted Buckner before he died--Milt Buckner's brother.

ctx.x: And J. C. Heard from that moment on became one of my protégés. And he used to have a problem of raising his tempos ... you know, he used to rush his tempos. But he went on to become one of the all-time greats as a percussionist, to be rated along with Jo Jones and those guys ; and played with all kinds of bands...Cab Calloway, Café Society, Jazz at the Philharmonic and I was so proud that one year I took him to Europe for a festival in Cannes and he...I took him to this festival in Cannes and we had Sidney Bechet…

And to hear him play with Dorothy Donegan was...she was fantastic and so was he, so...I think that you'd consider that... I'd consider it and classify it as a game of skill, have the two of them playing together, you know, as they did. As recently as 1975 I made some records with J. C. and Doc Cheatham, with Ted Buckner before he died--Milt Buckner's brother. And, who else did we have. We had...who did we have on bass?... DM: George Duvivier?
No, we didn't have George Duvivier, we had a guy they called "The Bruiser." I can't remember his name but I can
